descriptionChirho: Proper noun designating Bozrah (בָּצְרָה), a major city of Edom, identified with modern Buseirah in southern Jordan. The name means 'fortress' (related to בָּצַר, 'to fortify'). Appears as the home of Jobab son of Zerah, an Edomite king (Gen 36:33; 1 Chr 1:44), as a target of divine judgment against Edom (Isa 34:6, 63:1; Jer 49:13, 22; Amos 1:12), and in Jeremiah's oracle against Moab (Jer 48:24, though possibly a different Bozrah in Moab). All 8 occurrences across various prepositional constructions (בְּבָצְרָה 'in Bozrah,' מִבָּצְרָה 'from Bozrah,' absolute בָּצְרָה) refer to the same toponym. Multilingual glosses are consistent: Arabic بُصْرَة/بَصْرَةَ, Korean 보스라, Hindi बोस्रा, Spanish Botsrah/Bosra, German Bozra.
